sequence: Review protected recovery evidence and all outstanding slots before enabling production compilation.
Acquire the existing Mac scheduler mutex; refuse any unresolved prior management operation.
Compile an immutable plan against current state, with an external reviewed plan hash and expiry.
Dispatch once over existing SSH; controller owns runner/manual/submission locks in that order.
Retain the incumbent container and journal intent before every candidate effect.
On SSH loss, retain the Mac intent and mutex through bounded readback of the same operation. Never dispatch again because the reply was lost.
Validate exact candidate runtime and authenticated application/filter behavior, then require fresh monitor observations after activation.
Keep all processing holds. Serving success does not reconcile boot or enable workers.
Perform separately authorized ingress only when the replacement is ready; the existing ingress approval does not need repetition.
Return safe hashes and receipts. Keep protected content and signing material out of the relay.

rollback.target: the preserved exact incumbent container ID and configuration
forbidden: overwrite replacement writes with an old backup
limits: Serving rollback does not undo database migrations or reconcile data divergence.
New WebUI writes remain in the replacement volume and may not appear in the legacy interface.
An absent uncertain candidate, changed incumbent, changed hold or changed bound input requires explicit reconciliation.
After a terminal rollback, a new activation requires a newly reviewed plan, candidate names and journal.
If the Mac process dies and releases its mutex, the persistent pending intent must exclude future management effects until readback resolves it.

deadline_policy: Expiry and deadlines do not extend authority or permit bypassing missing evidence.
